citation: Hadjioannou, C. (2019). Angst as Evidence: Shifting Phenomenology's Measure. In C. Hadjioannou (Ed.), Heidegger on Affect (Philosophers in Depth) (pp. 69–104). Palgrave Macmillan. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-24639-6_4
thesis: Being and Time is not only an ontological revision of traditional metaphysics but a revision of phenomenology's own measure of epistemic justification. Both Husserl and Heidegger run transcendental, foundationalist projects grounding knowledge in evidence, but where Husserl anchors evidence in clear, distinct, apodictically certain originary intuition (internal to a reflecting consciousness), Heidegger relocates evidence in angst -- a pre-reflective, indeterminate, non-apodictic existential feeling that functions as the 'justifier of knowledge' for BT's interpretation of Dasein's thrown, finite, temporal structure. Heidegger is best described as a 'quasi-evidentialist': committed to some notion of evidential grounding, but incompatible with the mentalism and internalism built into Husserl's (and much of analytic epistemology's) construal of evidence. Contains no boredom-specific material; the chapter's contribution to this cluster is purely methodological.

sections.title: Unnumbered Introduction -- states the thesis; previews the roadmap; nominates angst as evidence for Dasein's finite, temporal structure
Phenomenology as a Foundationalist Project: Grounding Knowledge/Interpretation in Evidence -- Husserl and Heidegger as Kantian-style transcendental projects; resoluteness analogous to the epoché
Originary Intuition and Apodictic Certainty -- Husserl's Principle of All Principles; shift from adequation to apodicticity (Schmid's periodization)
Husserl's Mentalist Evidentialism -- via Berghofer, Husserl classed as a mentalist evidentialist in Conee & Feldman's technical sense
Heidegger's Alternative Beginning: Affective Evidence vs. Intuitive Evidence -- angst juxtaposed against Cartesian/Husserlian clarity-and-distinctness criteria
Care for Certainty: Science, Knowledge and Purification -- 1923/24 IPR lecture course; the Cartesian 'care for certainty' Husserl inherits
Criteria for Truth: Clarity and Distinctness -- Descartes' non-localized-pain example; moods fail the distinctness criterion
The Mangling of Evidence -- Husserl's care-for-certainty distorts intentionality and affective life; reflection as the distorting phenomenon (IPR 209, 220)
Evidence in Being and Time -- disposition/mood as 'methodologically significant in principle'; lack of mood never simply nothing
Angst: The Authentic Certainty of Resoluteness -- resoluteness 'exacts anxiety of oneself'; authentic Being-certain distinguished from apodictic present-at-hand certainty
Angst and Mentalist Evidentialism -- tripartite argument: (a) ontology over epistemology, (b) angst not a mental state, (c) angst not internal to a subject
Concluding Remark -- restates the radicalization-of-evidence thesis
Endnotes 1-14, incl. n.7 on Withy's methodological reading of angst and n.8's extended Befindlichkeit-translation excursus engaging Elpidorou & Freeman

readings.text: BT's ontological revision is inseparable from a methodological revision of what phenomenology accepts as evidence; the dedication to Husserl marks an intellectual honesty precisely because BT overturns Husserl's own method.

Both Husserl and Heidegger run transcendental/foundationalist projects grounding a priori conditions of meaning in evidence; Kant's 'epistemic conditions' have a hermeneutic analogue in Heidegger's 'conditions of interpretation' (Carman).

Resoluteness (Entschlossenheit) is methodologically analogous to Husserl's epoché/Principle of Evidence: both are the normative switch licensing reinterpretation and grounding transcendental knowledge, though what counts as evidence differs radically.
Husserl's Principle of All Principles: every originary presentive intuition is a legitimizing source of cognition; across his career the operative ideal shifts from adequation to apodicticity.

Following Berghofer, Husserl is a mentalist evidentialist in Conee & Feldman's technical sense: evidence determines justification, evidence consists of mental states, and one's ultimate evidence is internal to one's own experience.
Heidegger's rehabilitation of moods as ontological evidence is a deliberate juxtaposition against the Cartesian/Husserlian criteria of clarity, distinctness, and apodictic certainty.

Anxiety satisfies BT's own explicit methodological requirement (SZ 182) for a disclosive phenomenon exhibiting Dasein's primordial totality of Being 'in an elemental way'; Heidegger nominates anxiety by name for this role.

Heidegger's most sustained critique of Husserlian evidence is in the 1923/24 lecture course Introduction to Phenomenological Research (IPR), organized around a diagnosed 'care for certainty' inherited from Descartes via Husserl.

Descartes' clear-but-not-distinct unlocalized-pain example shows, on Heidegger's reading, that moods structurally fail the distinctness criterion and are excluded a priori from evidential status on the Cartesian/Husserlian model.

Husserl's care for certainty distorts both intentionality (reduced to theoretical Meinen) and affective/emotional life (analogized to acts of knowing); the reflective act grounding Husserlian evidence is what mangles affective phenomena.
In BT, disposition/mood is 'methodologically significant in principle' for the existential analytic; moods disclose Being-in-the-world as a meaningful whole, and lack of mood is never simply nothing.

Resoluteness 'exacts anxiety of oneself' and thereby achieves authentic certainty (Being-certain), a certainty Heidegger explicitly distinguishes from apodictic present-at-hand evidence, to which it does not belong at all.

Closing tripartite argument: (a) Heidegger rejects epistemology's/certainty's priority over ontology, so BT is only quasi-evidentialist; (b) angst is not a mental state (disposition, not state-of-mind); (c) angst is not internal to a bounded subject (contra Husserl's residual individualism, rationalism, internalism, per Crowell).

Overall verdict: BT is incompatible with mentalist evidentialism and internalism generally, while remaining committed to some notion of evidential grounding, without which the phenomenological project would collapse into unjustified assertion.

The everyday response to angst reinterprets it as fear of a determinate oncoming event, then dismisses that fear as weakness -- a double displacement banishing angst from the 'epistemological frame'; 'the they' polices this displacement.

Crowell's threefold characterization of what angst contests in Husserl -- residual individualism, rationalism (theoretism), and internalism -- supplies the vocabulary for why affective evidence is non-representationalist and not a forum internum.

concepts.gloss: the chapter's central category; for Husserl, originary presentive intuition; for Heidegger, angst -- the phenomenon that grounds/justifies interpretive-ontological claims

concepts.term: Originary intuition / Principle of All Principles
concepts.gloss: Husserl's claim that every originary presentive intuition is a legitimizing source of cognition, the foundation of phenomenological evidence
Husserl's mature ideal of evidence: the absolute unimaginableness of a state-of-affairs' non-being, replacing the earlier ideal of adequation
Conee & Feldman's category (via Berghofer): justification determined by quality of evidence, evidence = mental states, internal to the subject's mental life; applied to Husserl
Hadjioannou's own coinage for Heidegger's BT position: still committed to grounding claims in evidence/certainty, but incompatible with mentalism and internalism

concepts.term: Care for certainty (Sorge um die Gewissheit)
concepts.gloss: Heidegger's diagnosis, in the 1923/24 IPR lectures, of the Cartesian tendency organizing Husserl's phenomenology, prioritizing security over the matter itself
Heidegger's normative criterion functioning analogously to Husserl's epoché; achieves 'authentic certainty' by exacting anxiety of oneself
translated 'disposition' by Hadjioannou (against Macquarrie & Robinson's 'state-of-mind'); Aristotelian διάθεσις homology argued at length in n.8
mood; the basic way disposition is manifested; neither subjective nor objective, 'in-between' internal and external
anxiety; discloses Dasein face to face with the 'nothing', the possibility of impossibility of existence

interlocutors.name: Edmund Husserl
interlocutors.role: primary target text (Ideas I, Cartesian Meditations); the originary-intuition/apodictic-certainty model of evidence Heidegger radicalizes and displaces

interlocutors.name: Philipp Berghofer
interlocutors.role: contemporary epistemologist whose classification of Husserl as a mentalist evidentialist (2018 articles) Hadjioannou adopts and builds on

interlocutors.name: Taylor Carman
interlocutors.role: cited for the Kant/Heidegger 'epistemic conditions'/'hermeneutic conditions' analogy and for BT's interpretive aims (Carman 2003)

interlocutors.name: Steven Crowell
interlocutors.role: cited for evidential self-responsibility in BT's structure and for the threefold critique of Husserlian individualism/rationalism/internalism that angst contests (Crowell 2013)

interlocutors.name: Katherine Withy
interlocutors.role: cited (n.7) for reading angst as methodologically -- not merely ontologically/ethically -- significant; cluster-hub author (bor-sec-51)

interlocutors.name: Andreas Elpidorou & Lauren Freeman
interlocutors.role: extensively engaged in n.8's Befindlichkeit-translation excursus; their untranslated-term proposal is contested; Freeman's solo 2014 work cited in main text; cluster-hub authors (bor-sec-02, -03, etc.)

interlocutors.name: Daniel Dahlstrom
interlocutors.role: counted (with Carman and Wrathall) among scholars translating Befindlichkeit as 'disposition'; cluster/volume co-contributor whose own chapter follows immediately (bor-sec-49)

interlocutors.name: Stephen Mulhall
interlocutors.role: quoted for the claim that moods are revelatory of world and Dasein together, not merely of an inner state (Mulhall 1996)

interlocutors.name: Rene Descartes
interlocutors.role: genealogical source of the 'care for certainty' and clarity/distinctness criteria Husserl inherits; his own non-localized-pain example used against him/Husserl

interlocutors.name: Christos Hadjioannou (self-citations)
interlocutors.role: cites own prior work: Hadjioannou 2018 (Heidegger's critique of Husserl's reductive method), Hadjioannou 2013 (Befindlichkeit as Aristotelian διάθεσις), Hadjioannou 2015 (PhD thesis)

tensions.label: Mentalist evidentialism vs. quasi-evidentialism
tensions.poles: Husserl's evidence as internal, mental-state-based, apodictically certain (mentalist evidentialism) vs. Heidegger's evidence as pre-reflective, non-mental, relational, non-apodictic (quasi-evidentialism)

tensions.label: Befindlichkeit translation debate
tensions.poles: 'state-of-mind' (Macquarrie & Robinson) vs. 'findingness' (Haugeland) vs. 'situatedness' (Guignon) vs. 'affectedness/affectivity' (Dreyfus, Blattner, Crowell) vs. 'attunement' (Stambaugh) vs. left untranslated (Elpidorou & Freeman) vs. 'disposition' (Hadjioannou's own choice, with Carman, Dahlstrom, Wrathall)

tensions.label: Authentic (Being-certain) vs. apodictic (present-at-hand) certainty
tensions.poles: Husserlian apodictic certainty -- universal validity, indifferent, computable via originary intuition -- vs. Heideggerian authentic certainty -- finite, incomputable, non-apodictic, achieved through resoluteness's exacted anxiety
